summary: No Perlis-specific signal was identified in the source inventory: both sources record findings at national level only, so Perlis stands under Malaysia's federal framework and the national assessment for the country applies.
tangentialFactors: Both sources are national in scope. The enforcement actions, raids and court rulings they document are located in other Malaysian states, and neither source records an arrest, prosecution, raid or religious-authority action in Perlis.
localsOnly: Neither source identifies enforcement by Perlis religious authorities, a prosecution in the state, or any Perlis institution named in connection with the national crackdown. Residents of Perlis fall under the same federal and state framework described in the national assessment.
outOfScopeNotes: The text of Perlis's own Sharia enactment, the enforcement record of the state Islamic religious department in Perlis, and any Perlis arrest or prosecution figures are not present in the source inventory. Human Rights Watch and Justice for Sisters interviewed 73 LGBT people across Malaysia between 2018 and 2021 and name no Perlis case; the Human Dignity Trust country profile likewise records no Perlis-specific procedure or incident. Whether Perlis enforces its cross-dressing and same-sex intimacy provisions at a higher or lower rate than other states is unresolved on the available sources.
